page: Hetzner Cloud cpx32 is a shared-core virtual cloud server built on the x86_64 AMD EPYC architecture and virtualized via QEMU. The instance provides 4 vCPUs running at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz, backed by 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache per core cluster. System memory is configured at 8.0 GB, yielding 1.95 GB of RAM per vCPU. Storage is locally attached via a 160 GB NVMe SSD, and the platform includes no discrete GPU accelerators. The CPU configuration features hardware vector extensions including AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16 support.

Benchmark evaluations reveal top-quartile single-core compute throughput alongside stable memory write capabilities. The instance achieved a stress-ng single-core score of 3,040.68, placing it in the top 25% of tested systems, while the multi-core stress-ng result reached 12,106.51. In Geekbench testing, the server attained 1,818.0 in single-core and 5,716.0 in multi-core metrics. Memory performance reached 105.43 GB/sec in large-block uncached write tests. In contrast, static web serving throughput showed reduced efficiency, registering at 4.05 GB/sec, and 7B parameter LLM prompt processing reached 22.0 tokens/sec.

The 1:2 vCPU-to-memory profile delivers dense compute capacity for CPU-bound tasks, balanced against a shared-tenant execution model. Shared vCPU allocations introduce potential performance variability under prolonged peak multi-core saturation. However, the presence of fast local NVMe SSD storage mitigates I/O bottlenecks for data-intensive read and write operations. The instance is suited for CI/CD worker nodes, software compilation pipelines, testing environments, lightweight backend services, and intermediate batch processing.
description: Hetzner Cloud cpx32 is a virtual server instance powered by an AMD EPYC x86_64 processor under QEMU virtualization. It features 4 shared vCPUs clocked at 2.0 GHz, accompanied by 32 MB of L3 cache and support for modern vector instructions including AVX-512. The instance provisions 8.0 GB of system memory, matching a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, and includes 160 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage without discrete graphics accelerators. Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-core processing capabilities, recording 3,040.68 in stress-ng single-core tests and an uncached memory write throughput of 105.43 GB/sec, while static web serving throughput measures lower at 4.05 GB/sec. With shared CPU allocation, the server balances compute density and fast local NVMe storage against potential shared-host contention. The cpx32 server type is suitable for compilation pipelines, CI/CD runners, lightweight API endpoints, and intermediate batch processing tasks.
